source.title: Nanavira: consciousness is reflexive presence, not a thing requiring vimarśa
source.author: Codex/Hermes loop

source_span.locator: Notes on Dhamma — Viññāṇa, §d on reflexive presence

claims.claim_text: Consciousness (viññāṇa) is the presence of a phenomenon, and that presence is reflexively given. 'There is eye-consciousness — eye-consciousness is present reflexively.' Consciousness is not an entity or thing that requires an added property (vimarśa) to be sentient. It is the presence-of-phenomena, and presence as such is inherently reflexive. The immediate/reflexive presence distinction shows that reflexivity is built into the structure of experience, not added by a separate principle.
claims.hetu: consciousness is presence of phenomena, not an entity; presence is reflexively given
claims.sadhya: reflexivity is structural to Nanavira's account, not an added property
claims.vyapti_statement: If consciousness is presence and presence is reflexively given, then reflexivity is built into the structure of experience.

falsifier.condition: Show that Nanavira's 'reflexive presence' is compatible with a purely structural account that lacks sentience — i.e., that presence could be reflexively given without being experienced.
